note: Excerpt of the batch-159 progress ledger: the selection policy statement and the support-word mapping (JMdict entry ids, priority tags, and the row-specific exception reasons) for each new kanji.
selectionReason: The issue #60 rule selects up to ten absent Joyo kanji in frozen source-row order, with at least one support-word article per selected kanji. A qualifying support word uses JMdict news1, ichi1, spec1, or gai1; news2/spec2 do not qualify. The selected rows 135, 137, 139, 140, 146, 147, 148, 150, 152, and 153 are the first ten remaining Joyo rows after B158. Every new support word's other kanji already has a card. 又 is supported by the existing kana-headed articles または (spelling 又は, ichi1/news1) and また (spelling 又), under point 2 of the owner-accepted rule for B156 onward: an existing article, including a kana-headed one, is linked instead of adding a new one. Two rows take the rule's untagged route, each with a row-specific justification in its support mapping that must receive independent review: 后 (太后; the tagged 皇后 and 皇太后 need 皇, which has no card) and 吏 (官吏; no 吏 word carries a qualifying tag, and 官吏 has only news2/spec2). The 叔 row uses the untagged 伯叔 as an author's exception to point 2's preference for a tagged spelling, reported to the owner: the tagged spellings 叔父 and 叔母 have the シュク readings しゅくふ and しゅくぼ, but those readings carry no tag, and the tags belong to the whole-word readings おじ and おば. B156 applied the same interpretation to 伯 (伯仲). The exception is recorded in the 叔 support mapping and must receive independent review.

supportMappings.note: Existing kana-headed article. JMdict entry 1524930 tags only the reading また (ichi1/news1); the spelling 又 carries no priority tag, so this mapping is recorded as untagged. The qualifying support for 又 is または (spelling 又は).

supportMappings.exceptionReason: This row is an author's exception to the preference in point 2 of the issue #60 rule, reported to the owner for a decision. Under the letter of point 2, the tagged spellings 叔父 (entry 1607070) and 叔母 (entry 1607100), both ichi1/news1, are candidates: their readings しゅくふ and しゅくぼ, restricted to those spellings, use the KANJIDIC2 reading シュク and carry no irregular, rare, outdated, ateji, or gikun mark. They are not used because the tags in those entries belong to the whole-word readings おじ and おば, which the Joyo table lists in its notes for 叔 as special readings of 叔父 and 叔母; しゅくふ and しゅくぼ carry no priority tag; and an article headed 叔父 or 叔母 would teach おじ or おば as its primary reading, not シュク. B156 applied the same interpretation to 伯父 and 伯母 when it kept 伯仲 for 伯, and all three review families accepted that row. Every other candidate written with 叔, including 叔世 and the おじ/おば compounds such as 大叔父 and 叔父さん, is untagged. 伯叔 (entry 1474270) is untagged and is the Joyo table's only example for シュク; its other kanji 伯 has a card; its spelling and reading carry no irregular, rare, outdated, ateji, or gikun mark; and it backs the quizzed on reading シュク. JMdict glosses it “brothers; one's father's brothers”. If the owner prefers the letter of point 2, the fallback is an article headed 叔父 whose reading is しゅくふ. Keep this exception for independent review.

The candidates written with 后 that carry news1, ichi1, spec1, or gai1 cannot be used: 皇后 (entry 1280390, ichi1/news1) and 皇太后 (entry 1280450, news1) both need 皇, which has no card and is not in this batch; 午后 and 最后 are a rarely used and a search-only form of 午後 (1268990) and 最後 (1293810), whose tags belong to the 後 spellings; and 后 のち (1269330) lists 后 only as a search-only form. 后 きさき (1277320) carries only news2. The untagged route of the issue #60 rule therefore applies, with a row-specific justification. 太后 (entry 1787360) is untagged; its other kanji 太 has a card; its spelling and reading carry no irregular, rare, outdated, ateji, or gikun mark; and it backs the quizzed on reading コウ, the only reading in the Joyo table. Its gloss, “empress dowager; queen mother”, names both an empress and a queen, and Digital Daijisen defines it as a title for 太皇太后 or 皇太后. The untagged alternatives include 王后 (2014540, “queen”), 母后 (1783060, “empress dowager”), 后妃 and 后宮. Keep this explicit untagged exception for independent review.

No candidate written with 吏 carries news1, ichi1, spec1, or gai1 in the pinned snapshot, so the untagged route of the issue #60 rule applies, with a row-specific justification. 官吏 (entry 1211850) is the only 吏 entry with any priority marker (news2/spec2, treated as untagged); all other 吏 entries, including 吏 り (1549690, archaic) and 吏員 (1549700), are untagged. 官吏 is the second example for リ in the Joyo table; its other kanji 官 has a card; its spelling and reading carry no irregular, rare, outdated, ateji, or gikun mark, although JMdict marks its sense as dated; and it backs the quizzed on reading リ. JMdict glosses it “government official; public servant; civil servant”. 吏員 (“official”), the first Joyo example, and 能吏 (1470320), the third, are untagged. Keep this explicit untagged exception for independent review.
